newsitem.title: USA: 3DO posts Q3 profit, teams with Samsung.
newsitem.headline: 3DO posts Q3 profit, teams with Samsung.

text.p: 3DO Co on Wednesday reported a profit in its fiscal third quarter, after posting a loss in the same period the previous year, but its earnings of $2.9 million fell short of Wall Street forecasts.

3DO, a video game software developer, also said it agreed to set up a joint venture with Samsung Electronics Co Ltd to design specialized computer chips for consumer devices. Samsung will invest about $30 million in the venture.

The venture, yet to be named, will take over 3DO's development of chips for next-generation video game machines and develop graphic cards for personal computers, said Hugh Martin, 3DO president. With the joint venture, 3DO, once a developer of video game consoles, will complete an exit from the hardware business.

3DO, based in Redwood City, Calif., said it had profit of $2.9 million, or $0.10 a share, in the quarter ended December 31, compared with a loss of $19.1 million, or $0.74, in the same quarter a year ago.
Wall Street expected 3DO to earn $0.14 cents a share, according to a recent survey by First Call.
Third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $21.4 million from $8.9 million.

"We are pleased with the quarter," Martin said. "We think that over the last six months we've taken a lot of actions to streamline operations. We think expenses will even fall below the third quarter's."

Some of that streamlining reflected 3DO's decision to get out of the home video game machine business last year. The company is now concentrating exclusively on designing video games for personal computers and the Internet.
Martin said the business plan for the joint venture is not completed yet, but it likely will concentrate on making electronic components to improve the graphics capabilities of personal computers.
